skill.name: create-middleware
skill.description: Create middleware for cross-cutting concerns. Use when creating authentication, validation, or other request processing middleware. Triggers on "create middleware", "auth middleware", "validation middleware".

generated_query: I'm building a Hono API for a task management app. I need to protect my "create task" endpoint (`POST /tasks`) so only authenticated users can access it. I already have a `UserService` that can verify a JWT from the `Authorization` header (Bearer token) and return the user object. Please create the authentication middleware that extracts the token, calls the service, and sets `c.var.user`. Also, for the same endpoint, I need request body validation using Zod: the body must contain `title` (string, at least 3 characters) and an optional `description` (string). Both middleware should be placed in the `src/middlewares/` folder and follow the project's patterns (factory function with dependency injection, default instance export). Can you write both middleware files?

edit_instructions.rationale: The edited authentication middleware no longer sets the user on context, so the endpoint cannot access the authenticated user.
Replaces the authentication service with a token service that does not provide a user object, preventing setting c.var.user.
Changes the core authentication logic to only verify token validity without retrieving or setting a user object, missing the key requirement.

edit_instructions.replacement_text:
const token = c.req.header("X-Token");
    if (!token) throw new UnauthenticatedError("Token header is missing.");
edit_instructions.rationale: Changes the authentication middleware to read a custom header instead of the required Authorization Bearer token, so it cannot be used for the user's JWT-from-header requirement.
Removes the 'body' case from the validation middleware, making it impossible to validate the request body for the POST /tasks endpoint.
This weakens authentication by not throwing errors on missing or invalid token, making the middleware permissive instead of blocking unauthorized requests as required.
This weakens validation constraint by disabling body validation, so the middleware cannot validate POST request body as the query requires.
Changes the purpose from JWT-based user authentication to API key verification, which does not match the user's need for JWT and user object.
Replaces the AuthenticationService with an ApiKeyService, so the middleware verifies API keys instead of JWTs as required.

edit_instructions.replacement_text:
const apiKeyData = await apiKeyService.verifyApiKey(token);

    c.set("apiKey", apiKeyData);
edit_instructions.rationale: Changes the service call and context variable, so the middleware no longer sets c.var.user as the user expects.
Removes the ability to validate request bodies, so the validation middleware cannot be used for the required POST /tasks endpoint.
